title: dynamic-cohort-batcher-advisor-with-slo-eviction-and-anomaly-fencing
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a safe, automated advisor that generates per-cohort batching and caching config suggestions and applies them with SLO-aware limiters and anomaly fencing. The advisor should: analyze traffic cohorts, recommend batch/window sizes and cache policies, propose conservative KV cache pinning, and provide a safe apply path (shadow -> canary -> staged rollout) with automated rollback when latency/throughput SLO regressions are detected.
background: We already have human-driven batching recommendations and a set of runtime guardrails. Engineering and PMs want an automated advisor that reduces operator effort and captures tail risk when applying aggressive batch/cache configs. Recent experiments showed up to 28% token-cost reduction but introduced rare P99 latency spikes during traffic bursts. This ticket encodes the automation and safety plumbing to make those savings production-safe.
goals: 1) Produce conservative and aggressive config recommendations per cohort with estimated cost/latency impact. 2) Implement a safe apply pipeline with SLO gates and anomaly fencing. 3) Add observability and runbook links so SREs can debug and override. 4) Reduce manual rollout time for batching changes by 70% while keeping P99 latency regressions < 10% of baseline during rollout.
non-goals: Automated model quantization or kernel selection are out of scope for this ticket; those are handled by the compilation team.
proposed_solution_steps: 1) Cohort analysis service: ingest 7 days of traffic traces, cluster by request characteristics (prompt length, tokens, model, route, client tier) and surface top N cohorts.
2) Static simulator: run candidate configs (batch size, microwindow, KV cache TTL/pinning) against sampled traces to estimate cost and latency distributions (P50/P95/P99).
3) Config scorer: produce conservative and aggressive recommendations with expected savings and risk score. Use heuristics + learned model from past rollouts.
4) Safe apply pipeline: shadow apply -> canary (1%) -> staged ramp (1%,5%,20%,50%) with SLO gates at each step. SLO gates evaluate: P99 latency, error rate, throughput delta, and GPU tail metrics.
5) Runtime guardrails: per-cohort limiters (max_concurrency, in_flight_tokens_cap, batch_latency_budget) and SLO-aware routing that will route requests exceeding budgets to a fallback model/variant.

6) Anomaly detection and fencing: use EWMA + change-point detection on P99 and 95th-percentile request duration; quarantine cohort traffic when anomalies exceed thresholds for >3 minutes and open a rollback window.
7) Observability: generate a per-rollout dashboard with pre/post histograms, cohort breakdown, and quick links to logs and PRs.
8) Operator controls: manual pause/abort, adjust aggressiveness, and emergency circuit that immediately disables automated applies for a customer or route.
9) Post-apply evaluation: automatic A/B compare for 24 hours and a postmortem checklist if rollback triggered.
acceptance_criteria: Advisor can generate recommendations for >90% of active traffic cohorts within 10m of running simulation on 1 day of traffic sample.
Shadow apply path emits no routing changes and collects metrics for the rollout candidate.
Canary ramp is automated with SLO gates: if P99 latency increases by >10% or error rate increases by >0.5pp from baseline for two consecutive windows (60s windows), the rollout auto-rolls back.
Anomaly fencing automatically isolates cohorts if P99 > baseline*2 for a sustained 3+ minute interval and triggers rollback or traffic ejection to fallback variant.
Runbook created and linked in ticket; on-call can abort and will receive pager if automated rollback triggers for customer-impacting cohorts.
Unit and integration tests for scorer, simulator, and safe apply pipeline exist with coverage for boundary conditions.
Dashboard surfaces before/after cost delta and latency histograms per cohort.
Decrease manual rollout time for batching configs by >=70% in internal experiment.
No security-review blockers listed in the ticket (security_review_required=false).
implementation_notes: Key trade-offs: conservative recommendations sacrifice some cost savings for lower risk; aggressive recommendations should be clearly labeled and require operator opt-in. Limiters must be cheap to evaluate in the hot path; implement as token-limited counters and sliding-window EWMA in the serving proxies. Use a small in-process cache for cohort decisions with TTL to avoid extra RPCs.

2026-03-06: Simulator v0 ran against 1M requests; produced recommendation sets (conservative/aggressive). Observed a tail-case where aggressive batches increased 99th by 1.9x on bursty sequences.
2026-03-09: Implemented basic EWMA-based anomaly detector in staging and validated with synthetic spike tests. Early results look promising for detecting burst-induced tail spikes within 90s.
2026-03-10: Created dashboard template and linked design doc. Preparing PR for safe-apply controller (runtime/pull/3456).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: False positives in anomaly detector cause unnecessary rollbacks. Mitigation: require sustained breach (3 minutes) and cross-metric confirmation (P99 + error rate + GPU queue length).
Risk: Limiters add latency to hot path. Mitigation: keep limiter in proxy with O(1) checks and fall back to token bucket with local counters. Benchmark limiter <50us median cost.
Risk: Cohort churn leads to oscillation. Mitigation: add hysteresis and cooldown windows for cohort re-evaluation (default 30m).
Risk: Aggressive configs cause silent throughput degradation. Mitigation: require throughput delta checks and add canary rollout with throughput baseline gating.
